A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRIN research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original polymer-property prediction experiments, ablations, computational measurements and representation analyses in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including evaluations on six labeled datasets and an unlabeled-polymer representation analysis.

M1.justification: The repeat-unit augmentation, max-aggregation message passing, residual updates and sparsity objective in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GlassTemp, MeltingTemp, PolyDensity, O2Perm, EA and IP, plus the same 12,764 unlabeled polymers. The repeat-size test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments, including GAT and GraphGPS in Table 7 and augmented GCN/GIN comparisons in Tables 13–14.

E3.justification: The 60%/10%/30% data splits, augmentation procedures, R2 and RMSE metrics, model configurations, training budgets and testing procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: The augmentation-size and merge-ratio ablations, aggregation comparisons, baseline augmentation tests and embedding analyses are retained without revision (Figures 2–3, Table 5 and Appendix D).

E5.justification: Appendix B retains mean ± standard deviation reporting over three random initializations. No run-count, uncertainty-reporting or statistical-procedure changes appear elsewhere.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 11 retains cosine similarities of 0.672±0.119 for GCN, 0.903±0.060 for BFGCN and 0.999±0.000 for GRIN.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3, equations and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Correcting 'othes' to 'others' in Section 3.3.1 does not alter the argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about repetition invariance, MST alignment, minimal three-unit augmentation and benchmark outperformance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of extrapolation and augmentation results are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning labeled-data scarcity and additional computational cost, alongside the same applicability and future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Hardware, software versions, hyperparameters, sparsity warm-up, stopping rules and baseline implementation information remain unchanged in Appendix B. The new acknowledgement supplies no technical or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 38 references and unchanged research positioning in Section 2. Bibliography entries move across pages without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: v3 corrects 'othes' to 'others', removes the duplicated 'with' in Table 3's caption, adds a funding and institutional-support acknowledgement after the conclusion, and updates the version/date stamp.

P2.justification: The corrected Table 3 caption rewraps, and the acknowledgement shifts the bibliography layout across pages 10–12. All figures and table bodies retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a support acknowledgement and fixes two minor typos, providing small disclosure and editorial benefits. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and appendices remain unchanged; these limited edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
